scope: Source recognition only. Automatic dominant-language token from checkpoint language detector, no listener language labels. Mixedcode mode enabled uniformly, matched no-marker control. No classifier/routing acceptance.
decoding: Full20s, FP16/SDPA T4, greedy440 per published token budget, batch1; same detectedlang for both prefixes, no tasktranslation.
limitations: Development clips with partial/unclear source references; no common-script WER or fullbilingualmeaning gate; originaluncertainties remain excluded. AutoLID setup not publisher specifiedlanguage benchmark.
acceptance: Any checked substantive loss or script failure rejects tested configuration; visually mixed output alone cannot pass.

comparison.method: Agent clear-span comparison against frozen listener wording/meaning; no direct audio perception, complete mixed-script reference or full Hindi translation adjudication.

automatic_mode.strategy: Checkpoint language detector selects prefix; mixedcode marker is enabled uniformly without a manual mixed-language classifier.
automatic_mode.interpretation: Coarse labels agree with listener English versus Hindi-English on these four cases. This is not representative automatic-language-routing validation.
automatic_mode.precision: FP16 from F32 checkpoint, finite parameters verified; no BF16 equivalence claim.

source_findings.blind-10: Both modes retain most clear English discussion, technical-looking terms, uncertainty and negation. Identical parsed outputs, incomplete reference; no full-window WER.
source_findings.blind-35: Both modes preserve Atlas and list-review purpose but substitute sign-of-responsibility for checked signup responsibility. Mixedcode also renders some fillers in Devanagari. Neither fixes this substantive English-control error. Unknown pre-release event remains unadjudicated.
source_findings.diagnostic-30-50: Mixedcode preserves clear date and English travel question/answer; no-marker control degrades the question into phonetic/garbled wording. English ordinary words are Latin in mixedcode; location names remain Devanagari. Uncertain opening and disputed probably excluded.
source_findings.blind-85: Mixedcode substantially improves English-Latin token-pricing/model-choice clause compared with previous recognizers and no-marker output. Hindi wording/opening amount/billing remain unverified; no full bilingual meaning pass.

source_decision.reason: Meaningful script/question preservation improvement, but signup error persists and only partial development references exist. Do not confuse improved formatting with complete fidelity.

rendering_metadata.source: Trelis auto_mixedcode outputs only; no human reference or correction.
rendering_metadata.policy: Translate the following segment into English, without additional explanation.

rendering_followup.scope: Four unchanged HY translations of Trelis mixedcode output only; no human corrections, vocabulary hints or translated references. Performed because source script/question preservation improved.
rendering_followup.confirmed_failure: On the checked opening, Trelis source retains the English destination question, but HY removes question form and adds an unsupported interpretation linking the date to the destinations. Failure is therefore independently visible in the rendering stage, not solely inherited source garbling.
rendering_followup.other_limits: English technical term changes need adjudication. Atlas source error is inherited and cannot be credited as repaired. Later mixed Hindi meaning/amount/billing remain unscored; actor resolution of ambiguous pronouns is not treated as checked truth.

completion.limit: EOS and keyword coverage do not establish semantic completeness.

comparison.decision: Keep Trelis mixedcode as a source-recognition candidate, not a release choice. Reject tested Trelis→HY pipeline on confirmed rendering question loss plus remaining source error. No product deployment.

runtime.limitation: Short batch1 sampled coexistence only, not sustained queue/caption capacity.
